criteria.formula: 100 * (Integrated Energy Factor / (1.8175 - 0.0006 * Certified capacity) - 1) if Certified capacity <= 25, else 100 * (Integrated Energy Factor / (2.0424 - 0.0001 * Certified capacity) - 1)
criteria.label: IEF vs same-class models

criteria.formula: certified capacity (pints/day) x 0.473 L per pint / certified IEF (L/kWh) x 1,095 / 24 (DOE's annual dehumidification hours, 10 CFR 430 subpart B appendix X1) x EIA U.S. average residential price x 5
criteria.label: 5-year electricity cost

criteria.formula: 100 pints x 0.473 L per pint / certified IEF (L/kWh) x EIA U.S. average residential price (no operating hours: it depends only on IEF and the rate)
criteria.label: Electricity cost per 100 pints removed

method: We fitted two straight lines of certified IEF on certified capacity, one for portable spec sets up to 25 pints a day and one above (ENERGY STAR's efficiency classes up to 25 and from 25.01 to 50 pints a day, with IEF floors of 1.70 and 2.01 L/kWh), over every portable ENERGY STAR dehumidifier spec set certified at 12 pints a day or more (few certified sets and a unit-typo listing below that), then took the models furthest above their own class's line. The 25-pint step decides much of the order: from 25.01 pints the floor is 2.01, so a unit just above 25 pints that sits on that floor scores below its class line and can rank below a smaller unit with a lower IEF, even though it removes more water at a higher IEF; to compare across the two classes, use the cost per 100 pints column, which does not depend on the class. The score is that distance alone; raw IEF and capacity are shown, not scored. The five-year electricity cost is shown for each (yearly energy computed from certified capacity and IEF at DOE's 1,095 dehumidifying hours a year x current EIA U.S. average residential price x 5; we do not use the listed yearly figure because for some listings it does not match their own capacity and IEF).
name: The most energy-efficient portable dehumidifiers against their ENERGY STAR class
scoring: each value scored against the best on the page (best = 1), times its weight; total out of 100

excluded.why: below 12 pints a day (about the 5th percentile of all certified portable sets, 10.2, before this filter) the certified sets are few and include a unit-typo listing (Ludatido PD10C2-25 lists 1.91 pints, the same number as its IEF; its 264 kWh a year implies about 23), so they are left out of the class fits and the ranking

selection.label: IEF vs its class line
selection.merge: listings with identical certified values on all 11 reported fields

ties.rule: equal scores share a rank; the scores differ only after the first decimal (95.368, 95.365 unrounded), and within the rank products are listed by that unrounded score
